gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hedvig-letters-sa: Chunky retro charm, pinched and friendly, from Junegull. Hedvig Letters Sans follows with wide-open curves and small letters that nearly match its capitals, a lighter sans-serif counterpoint.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-heebo: Heebo has a tall central band of text and curves that stop short instead of closing. Heebo's open shapes sit against Junegull's pinched, wire-like heading, so enlarge the body font a touch if the heading starts to dominate.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hind-guntur: Friendly and a little retro, Junegull pinches every curve shut, while Hind Guntur stays modern with wide gaps and tall lowercase like stamped metal. Closed against open is the whole story.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hind-madurai: Junegull is all pinched, cast-iron swagger, with lowercase standing as tall as its capitals and no thick-thin flicker. Hind Madurai opens its s curves wide, and lines hold together smoothly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri hums along at constant line weight, its rounds gapped like a cracked bangle. Hind Siliguri would carry a long passage with a gentle bump from small letters to capitals, no fuss in sight.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hind-vadodara: Junegull is retro and pinched, with a lowercase built like cast iron capitals. Hind Vadodara counters with spacious terminal gaps and tall open bowls, a plain sans that does the quiet work while Junegull makes the noise.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-huninn: Junegull pinches every curve into a retro, friendly squeeze. Huninn lets its s terminals stay clear of the body, with lowercase rising close to cap height, so the sans reads modern beneath the closed heading.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-inter-tight: Pinched curves and cast-iron lowercase give Junegull its retro, friendly grin. Inter Tight brings modern, rope-like lines with tails held well back, and the closed-versus-open difference is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and approachable, with a gaping c and a middle band so tall the line looks stocky. Karla sits under Junegull's retro, friendly heading, which has no flared ends, just pinched joints.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-kedebideri: Junegull builds every letter from one width of stroke, pinching its curves shut. Kedebideri, a sans-serif, does the opposite and stays open and inviting, with a skyward x-height; Junegull grabs attention while Kedebideri carries the text.
